message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"16","text":"Nevertheless, all of you should know that the bishop labors more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, take your place at the head as a helper to each person, as far as you are able, having taken upon yourself the cares of everyone. Hence I know that, in your undertaking to administer, I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and bear it nobly, knowing that when you have reached the harbor of rest, God will repay you with the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because you undertook the greater toil for the salvation of all. Thus, if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise arising from injustice, but through righteous administration to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κάμνοντα","chosen":"labors","rationale":"The verb denotes strenuous or wearisome labor."},{"source_quote":"προκαθέσθητι βοηθός","chosen":"take your place at the head as a helper","rationale":"The wording combines a leading or presiding position with service as a helper."},{"source_quote":"τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι","chosen":"in your undertaking to administer","rationale":"The selected interpretation takes Clement as undertaking the administration, while the competing infinitival analysis remains disclosed as unresolved."},{"source_quote":"ἀναφαίρετον μισθόν","chosen":"an inalienable reward","rationale":"The adjective describes a reward that cannot be taken away."},{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ ἄκρον δικαιοσύνην","chosen":"righteousness carried to the utmost","rationale":"The expression depicts righteousness extending to its furthest point."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ χριστοῦ","chosen":"from the Messiah","rationale":"Χριστός functions independently as a title here rather than as part of a personal-name construction."},{"source_quote":"θηρεύειν ἔπαινον","chosen":"to hunt for ... praise","rationale":"The rendering preserves the verb’s explicit hunting image and its force of active pursuit."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς","issue":"The infinitival construction remains syntactically uncertain. The translation takes σέ as the subject associated with ἀναδέξασθαι and οἰκονομεῖν as what Clement undertakes, so that the speaker receives a favor through Clement’s undertaking. Alternatively, the speaker may be the understood subject of ἀναδέξασθαι, with σὲ οἰκονομεῖν as its complement: the speaker undertakes to have Clement administer. The supplied reading is preserved, and neither analysis demonstrates textual corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"’σωτηρίας","issue":"The supplied print places a raised apostrophe before σωτηρίας although no elision is apparent. Omitting it would be an orthographic normalization and would not change the translated meaning.","proposed_reading":"σωτηρίας","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"17","text":"After saying these things and more than these, he again looked toward the multitude and said, “And you also, my beloved brothers and fellow servants, yield in every respect to the one presiding over truth, knowing this: whoever grieves this man has not received the Messiah, with whose chair he has been entrusted; and as one who has not received the Messiah, he will be reckoned as having rejected the Father. Therefore, he will be cast out of the good kingdom. For this reason, strive to come to every gathering, so that you may not, as deserters, incur a charge of sin because of the commander’s discouragement. Therefore, above all else, all of you should give thought to his interests, knowing that, because of each of you, the evil one wages war against him alone with greater hostility. So strive to continue in affection toward him and goodwill toward one another, and to obey him, so that he too may be relieved and you may be able to be saved.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"σύνδουλοι","chosen":"fellow servants","rationale":"The term presents the brothers as sharing the status and allegiance of servants."},{"source_quote":"προκαθεζομένῳ ἀληθείας","chosen":"the one presiding over truth","rationale":"The participle denotes occupying the leading seat or presiding position, with truth as its sphere."},{"source_quote":"χριστόν","chosen":"the Messiah","rationale":"The first occurrence functions independently as a title."},{"source_quote":"χριστὸν","chosen":"the Messiah","rationale":"The second occurrence likewise functions independently as a title rather than within a personal name."},{"source_quote":"καθέδραν","chosen":"chair","rationale":"The literal chair represents the entrusted teaching and governing office while preserving the source image."},{"source_quote":"λειποτάκται","chosen":"deserters","rationale":"This is a military term for those who abandon their assigned rank or post."},{"source_quote":"ταξιάρχου","chosen":"commander","rationale":"The military title continues the image introduced by the reference to deserters."},{"source_quote":"ἐπακούειν","chosen":"to obey","rationale":"In this exhortation, the verb conveys heedful compliance rather than merely hearing."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"’ὡς","issue":"The supplied print places a raised apostrophe before ὡς without an evident elision or syntactic function. Omitting it would be an orthographic normalization and would not affect the translation.","proposed_reading":"ὡς","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"18","text":"But you should also understand some things on your own, because he cannot speak openly on account of the plots. For example, if he is hostile to someone, do not wait for him to say, “Do not associate with this person.” Instead, prudently follow his intention, becoming enemies of those to whom he is hostile and not associating with those with whom he does not associate, so that each person, pressing his claim to have everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him and heeding his discourse. But if anyone remains a friend to those to whom he is hostile and speaks with those with whom he does not associate, he himself is also one of those who want to destroy the church. For although he is joined with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose, he is against you—far worse than the manifest enemies from outside, scattering those inside under the guise of friendship.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐν φανερῷ","chosen":"openly","rationale":"The expression contrasts public or unconcealed speech with what must be inferred because of plots."},{"source_quote":"προσαμιλλᾶσθαι","chosen":"associate with","rationale":"The verb can denote engaging or contending with someone, but the surrounding references to friendship and conversation support a relational sense."},{"source_quote":"βουλήματι","chosen":"intention","rationale":"The noun denotes the leader’s purpose or will, which the audience is expected to discern."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν","chosen":"pressing his claim to have everyone as friends","rationale":"The middle participle conveys asserting or pressing a claim, not merely seeking an outcome."},{"source_quote":"ὁμιλίας","chosen":"discourse","rationale":"The noun here refers to speech, conversation, or instruction that is to be heeded."},{"source_quote":"γνώμῃ","chosen":"purpose","rationale":"The term denotes inward judgment or intention, contrasted with bodily presence."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἔξωθεν φαινομένων ἐχθρῶν","chosen":"the manifest enemies from outside","rationale":"The rendering preserves both their evident enmity and their position outside, in contrast with those inside."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ δοκούσης φιλίας","chosen":"under the guise of friendship","rationale":"The participle marks the friendship as seeming or apparent rather than genuine."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν διαλλάττων","issue":"The antecedent of αὐτόν is not explicit. It may refer to the presiding leader or to an alienated person, producing materially different accounts of the reconciliation. The active διαλλάττων may mean reconciling the referent, winning him over, or effecting reconciliation with him. The translation retains the neutral pronoun and selects “reconciling” provisionally; the supplied wording does not settle the relationship.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας","issue":"The antecedent of αὐτοῦ is not explicit. The translation provisionally connects it with the presiding leader, but it could instead continue another referent from the preceding reconciliation clause. This is an interpretive uncertainty, not evidence of defective transcription.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"19","text":"After saying these things, there in the midst before everyone, he laid his hands on me and urged me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are here with me, I charge you: whenever I depart from this life here—as is owed to me—send James, the Lord’s brother, a concise written account, reaching back even to your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, listening to the words and deeds proclaimed by me from city to city. Then, toward the end, do not hesitate also to make known the cause of my death, as I foretold. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that I have piously paid what I was inevitably bound to suffer. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me the teacher’s chair was not entrusted to an unlearned man who is ignorant of life-giving words and does not know the church’s rule. For misleading discourse destroys the souls of the crowds who hear it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐδυσώπησεν","chosen":"urged","rationale":"The verb means to prevail upon or strongly entreat someone."},{"source_quote":"σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον","chosen":"send James, the Lord’s brother, a concise written account","rationale":"The second σέ is provisionally treated as a resumptive accusative subject of the infinitive, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with it; it need not make Clement the object being sent."},{"source_quote":"λογισμῶν","chosen":"thoughts","rationale":"The noun denotes thoughts, considerations, or reasonings extending back to Clement’s childhood."},{"source_quote":"κηρυχθέντων","chosen":"proclaimed","rationale":"The participle grammatically applies to both the words and the deeds, an unusual coordination retained in English."},{"source_quote":"πρόφασιν","chosen":"cause","rationale":"The noun can mean cause, occasion, or pretext; the requested account of Peter’s death supports “cause.”"},{"source_quote":"πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν","chosen":"I was inevitably bound to suffer","rationale":"Πάντως reinforces the certainty or inevitability of the necessary suffering."},{"source_quote":"ἀπεδόμην","chosen":"I have ... paid","rationale":"The aorist middle presents the necessary suffering as an obligation rendered or discharged."},{"source_quote":"κανόνα","chosen":"rule","rationale":"The noun denotes an authoritative norm or standard and need not refer to a later fixed collection of writings."},{"source_quote":"πλάνος","chosen":"misleading","rationale":"The adjective characterizes the discourse as leading its hearers astray."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν","issue":"The printed period separates the infinitive from the finite verb that most naturally governs it. The translation construes the words together while preserving the period as an editorial feature of the supplied edition; this punctuation does not by itself demonstrate textual corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν καὶ ὡς ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς μέχρι τοῦ νῦν συνώδευσάς μοι, ἐπακούων τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων, ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς","issue":"The extended request moves from Ἀξιῶ σε through ὅπως and ὁπόταν into an accusative-and-infinitive construction, then concludes with δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς. The second σέ can resume the earlier accusative as the subject of διαπέμψαι, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with it, but that analysis does not by itself settle how ὅπως, both infinitives, and the concluding prohibition are related. The translation gives the probable practical sense without altering the supplied wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν","issue":"The translation takes the first οὐκ as negating the entire described alternative: the chair was not entrusted to a man characterized as unlearned, ignorant of life-giving words, and not knowing the church’s rule. The grammatical scope of that first negation across the coordinated descriptions remains loose, while the later οὐκ explicitly negates εἰδώς and is preserved as “does not know.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς","issue":"The printed period interrupts the description before οὐκ εἰδώς. The translation treats the participle as continuing the description while retaining the period as an editorial feature; the punctuation alone is not evidence of textual corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20","text":"Therefore I, my lord James, when he had said these things and I had given my promise, did not hesitate, as I had been commanded, to arrange under headings the greater part of the discourses from city to city, which had already been written to you beforehand and sent by him in books, as a kind of reminder, and in this form to send them to you, giving the work the title “Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings during His Sojourns.” But I will begin to set it out as I was commanded.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑποσχόμενος","chosen":"I had given my promise","rationale":"The participle records Clement’s promise before describing his prompt fulfillment of it."},{"source_quote":"τὸ πολὺ","chosen":"the greater part","rationale":"The expression denotes the bulk or most of the material rather than necessarily all of it."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ κεφαλαίων","chosen":"under headings","rationale":"The phrase refers to principal points or summary headings used to organize an epitome."},{"source_quote":"σημείου χάριν","chosen":"as a kind of reminder","rationale":"Literally involving a sign or marker, the phrase describes the summary as an aid to recognition or recollection."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων","chosen":"Preachings during His Sojourns","rationale":"The selected title associates the preachings with Peter’s stays or visits, while the adjectival relationship and alternative local or public sense remain unresolved."},{"source_quote":"ἐκτιθέναι","chosen":"set it out","rationale":"The verb marks the transition from the prefatory letter to presenting the promised material."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐπιγράψαντα","issue":"The accusative participle is syntactically marked with the first-person subject of οὐκ ὤκνησα. It may agree with an understood accusative subject of the dependent infinitives. The nominative ἐπιγράψας would be a conjectural normalization, not an established correction to the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"ἐπιγράψας","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή","issue":"The adjective ἐπιδημίων directly qualifies κηρυγμάτων, but its contextual force remains uncertain. It may describe preachings delivered during Peter’s sojourns or visits, preachings associated more generally with those visits, or local or public preachings. The translation provisionally selects the sojourn sense without treating the supplied wording as corrupt.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
